To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the use of a large amount of data for language modeling is beneficial for the task of ASR; (b) the selection process we describe is effective in improving the acoustic coverage of the TED-LIum corpus, while keeping the quality of the data high.

(1) using selected data to estimate LMs is beneficial, (2) using selected data for acoustic data selection is also beneficial, and (3) using selected data is more beneficial than using unselected data.

1) we were able to improve the quality of the LMs we estimated for the TED-LIum corpus; 2) the selected data we added to the TED-LIU corpus are of high quality, and can be used to improve the performance of automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems; and 3) our selected data are useful to improve the performance for a number of tasks, including ASR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: (1) the use of open-source tools for language modeling, (2) the selection of new acoustic data, and (3) the use of the selected data for speech recognition.
